source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 6.

sections.heading: 1. Objects and Materials
points: Every **object** is made of one or more **materials** (e.g. a chair may be of wood, plastic or metal).
The **same object** can be made from different materials, and the **same material** can make many objects.
Materials are chosen for their **properties** (a cooking pot needs metal that conducts heat; a raincoat needs waterproof plastic).

sections.heading: 2. Properties of Materials
points: **Appearance / lustre:** shiny (**lustrous**, e.g. metals) vs dull.
**Hardness:** hard (iron) vs soft (cotton, sponge).
**Solubility:** soluble (salt, sugar in water) vs insoluble (sand, chalk).
**Float or sink** in water (linked to density): wood/oil float; stone/iron sink.
**Transparency:** transparent (glass), translucent (butter paper, frosted glass), opaque (wood, metal).
**Attraction to magnets** and **heat/electric conduction** are also properties.

sections.heading: 3. Soluble and Insoluble; Miscible and Immiscible
points: **Soluble** substances dissolve in water (salt, sugar); **insoluble** do not (sand, chalk powder).
**Miscible** liquids mix completely (water + milk); **immiscible** liquids do not (oil + water — form separate layers).
Water is called a **universal solvent** because it dissolves many substances.

sections.heading: 4. Grouping Materials
points: Materials are **grouped** by shared properties to study and use them better.
Grouping helps in **choosing the right material** for a purpose and in **organising** knowledge.
Example: grouping by 'floats/sinks', by 'transparent/opaque', or by 'soluble/insoluble'.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Objects are made of materials; one material → many objects, and vice versa.
Properties: lustre, hardness, solubility, density (float/sink), transparency, magnetism, conduction.
Transparent (glass) → translucent (butter paper) → opaque (wood).
Soluble = dissolves (salt/sugar); insoluble = doesn't (sand).
Miscible liquids mix (water+milk); immiscible don't (oil+water).
Water = universal solvent.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Translucent** (partly lets light through, e.g. butter paper) is between **transparent** and **opaque**.
**Soluble/insoluble** is about solids dissolving; **miscible/immiscible** is about liquids mixing.
Floating or sinking depends on **density** relative to water, not simply on weight.
**Lustre** = shine; most metals are lustrous.
